idiom_name: duck-typed view object (optional typing.Protocol) + plain presenter object
implementation_notes: Python has no interfaces at runtime: any object with the required methods is a view, so the classic abstract view hierarchy collapses into a small class (or a Protocol used only for static checking), the presenter is a plain object receiving view and model, and a test double is a tiny class or a mock. Duck typing and typing.Protocol replace the interface, and GUI toolkits only need to forward gestures - tkinter's command callbacks or Qt signals call presenter methods, while the presenter itself imports no toolkit. Keep the classic Protocol-typed form when several views must conform and type checkers should enforce it; for a single screen, plain methods and a conformance test are enough. This is the idiomatic route because the structure the classic pattern spends a class hierarchy on is free in Python.
pitfalls: Protocols are not enforced at runtime: a view missing a method fails only when the presenter calls it, so keep one conformance test against the real view class.

View and presenter holding bound methods of each other create reference cycles; the collector handles them, but explicit detach (clearing the attribute) avoids surprises with __del__ and long-lived screens.
tkinter callbacks only run inside mainloop() on the main thread; a presenter invoked from a worker thread must publish updates via root.after or a queue.
